reason: The cited evidence shows Cu-rich regions forming and persisting in a related HEA system, supporting the idea of segregation-driven liquid formation, but it does not directly address nanoparticle-specific behavior, controlled quenching vs. slow cooling, or quantitative melting point shifts, leaving several key premises only indirectly supported.
premises: Cu-rich regions in FeNiCrCoCu can form during heat treatment and act as liquid nucleation sites
Compositional segregation persists after high-temperature exposure and is not eliminated by homogenization
Localized Cu enrichment lowers the local melting point relative to the bulk alloy
Segregated nanoparticles will show a lower melting onset and broader transition than homogeneous ones
Rapid quenching yields homogeneous nanoparticles while slow cooling induces measurable segregation
